Stewart and his allies were successful in legitimatizing patents in pharmaceutical manufacturing but were unsuccessful in their efforts to reconcile medical science with commercial interests.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Stewart and Davis were successful in their efforts to legitimate patents in pharmaceutical manufacturing, but in the process they undermined the very ethical basis for patent protection that they had hoped to preserve.

Stewart's efforts to legitimate the commercial introduction of pharmaceuticals helped create a situation in which the pharmaceutical industry was no longer dependent on the medical profession to introduce its new drugs to the public.
Stewart's work was a significant step toward the development of the pharmaceutical industry as we know it today.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patents have been used as a tool to promote the development and introduction of new drugs, even though many of the ethical issues surrounding their use remain unsettled to this day.
patent rights in pharmaceuticals are a relatively recent invention that have only come to exist in the form we know today in the last 150 years.
